FINDING_ID: R7_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.78  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58  
DESCRIPTION: `reassign()` accepts `round_idx` but never uses it. Failure-history penalty is documented as depending on round (`phi_hist(m, r-1)`), yet the implementation aggregates the entire lifetime history with no round alignment, no windowing, and no validation that exactly one failure datum exists per prior round. This creates semantic drift between the API contract and implementation: callers can reasonably assume reassignment for round `r` uses history through `r-1`, but the method actually uses whatever booleans happen to have been appended, possibly including duplicate entries, missing rounds, or out-of-order records. That can bias COL selection and make runs non-reproducible across different call sequences.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either remove `round_idx` and document penalty as lifetime mean over recorded events, or enforce round-indexed history storage, e.g. `Dict[str, Dict[int, bool]]`, and compute penalty only from rounds `< round_idx` with explicit validation of duplicates/missing data.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: R7_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.74  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.61  
DESCRIPTION: `assign()` can silently produce an invalid role map when `models` contains duplicate `model_id` values. This is broader than the already-found “no uniqueness validation” issue because the failure mode is specifically inconsistent internal cardinality: `models_list` may contain N entries, but `scores` and `role_map` are keyed by ID and collapse duplicates. The PM/COL/PAR assignment steps operate over model objects, yet writes into `role_map` overwrite prior entries under the same key, so the returned assignment can contain fewer roles than models with no error. This violates the intended mapping `rho : M -> Roles` because `M` is treated as a sequence of model objects during assignment but as a set of IDs in storage.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Fail fast in `assign()` by validating `len({m.model_id for m in models_list}) == len(models_list)` before any scoring, and define uniqueness as a hard precondition in the public contract.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: R7_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.67  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.49  
DESCRIPTION: `reassign()` does not validate that `active_models` is a subset of the known model universe. Unknown IDs are partially ignored: they enter `remaining_ids`, participate in the “do we have remaining models?” logic, but later disappear if `next((m ...), None)` returns `None`. This creates a misleading success path where caller bugs are masked and the returned map omits requested active models without raising. Prior reviewers noted silent skipping generally, but the missed area-specific bug is that unknown IDs can perturb control flow before being dropped, including hysteresis eligibility via `len(remaining_ids) >= 2`.  
PROPOSED_FIX: At method entry, compute `known_ids = {m.model_id for m in self._models}` and raise `ValueError` if `active_models - known_ids` is non-empty. Then derive `remaining_ids` from validated IDs only.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: R7_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.63  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.56  
DESCRIPTION: `reassign()` can assign PAR roles to models that were never successfully scored in the current pass. If `remaining_ids` includes a known model whose score computation fails indirectly at lookup time because the model was omitted from `models_for_scoring` reconstruction or because future `ModelSpec` evolution makes the reconstruction incomplete, that model is skipped for COL scoring (`continue`) but still assigned `Role.PAR` in the final loop. This means the returned role map may contain participants that were not admissible under the current scoring basis. In the current artifact this is reachable whenever `model is None` for a known ID due to representation mismatch.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Build a validated `scorable_models: Dict[str, ModelSpec]` once, derive `remaining_ids` from its keys, and raise on any active known ID that lacks a scorable model instance rather than silently downgrading it to PAR.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: R7_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.58  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.44  
DESCRIPTION: The return type and state semantics of `reassign()` are inconsistent with encapsulation expectations: it returns the same mutable `dict` instance stored in `self.role_map`. External code can retain the returned object and mutate internal state without going through any class method. Prior findings covered public mutability in general, but the missed specific bug is aliasing at the method boundary: even if `role_map` were later wrapped or reassigned internally, this method currently leaks the live backing object on every call.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Return a defensive copy, e.g. `return dict(new_map)`, and store an internal immutable mapping or expose a read-only view/property for consumers.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: R7_F006  
SEVERITY: 0.52  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.41  
DESCRIPTION: `validate_k1()` and `validate_homogeneous()` invoke `RoleAssignment.assign(...)` directly rather than `cls.assign(...)` or a passed implementation handle. As static methods on the class they are nominally validators for the current implementation, but in subclassed or alternative deployments they hard-code the base class and will validate the wrong constructor/logic. This weakens the advertised reduction-property checks as an extensibility and testability mechanism.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Convert validators to `@classmethod` and call `cls.assign(...)`, or move them to standalone test helpers that explicitly target `RoleAssignment`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: R7_F007  
SEVERITY: 0.61  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.53  
DESCRIPTION: `get_ordering()` exposes scores for all models in `capability_scores`, including inactive or logically removed ones, with no way to request ordering over the current active assignment state. Because `reassign()` changes only `role_map` and not the score universe, consumers may mistakenly interpret `get_ordering()` as current operational ordering. Prior stale-score findings covered non-refresh; the additional flaw is API ambiguity: even with refreshed scores, the method has no active-set filter and can rank models that are unavailable for dispatch.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either document it as “full-pool historical ordering” or add an `active_only: bool = False` parameter using current active state tracked explicitly by the object. Prefer separating `get_pool_ordering()` from `get_active_ordering()`.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: R7_F008  
SEVERITY: 0.46  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.36  
DESCRIPTION: `record_failure()` permits unbounded growth of `_failure_history` lists with no retention policy, despite reassignment only using the mean. For long runs this accumulates O(rounds × models) booleans when a constant-space `(fail_count, total_count)` representation would suffice. This is not a correctness flaw for small runs but is an avoidable memory and serialization burden in a manager component expected to operate across many rounds.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Replace per-round boolean lists with compact counters or a bounded/weighted history structure if recency is needed. If full audit history is required, separate audit logging from the statistics used for reassignment.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: R7_F009  
SEVERITY: 0.57  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.47  
DESCRIPTION: `assign()` stores `_models = models_list` by reference to the same `ModelSpec` objects provided by the caller. Even if the list container is copied, the model objects are not. If `ModelSpec` is mutable, external mutation after assignment can retroactively change future reassignment behavior without any audit trail, bypassing the intended lock-in of initial pool characteristics. This is especially relevant because live updates are supposed to flow through the explicit `live_fingerprints` parameter.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Require `ModelSpec` to be immutable (`@dataclass(frozen=True)`) or deep-copy model specs on ingest. Document that post-assignment external mutation is unsupported and enforce it structurally.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: R7_F010  
SEVERITY: 0.43  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.33  
DESCRIPTION: Cross-component concern [unverified from this area]: `RoleAssignment.reassign()` uses `active_models` as a plain set of IDs and separately accepts `live_fingerprints`, but there is no local check that the live fingerprints correspond to the same round/state snapshot as the active set. If `DynamicManager` or `FailureHandler` supplies mismatched snapshots, reassignment can score one round’s capabilities against another round’s liveness. The interface encourages torn reads across components.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Accept a single immutable snapshot object containing `round_idx`, active IDs, and fingerprints captured atomically by the orchestrator, and validate snapshot round consistency.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

Definitive stance: the main newly surfaced issues are unused `round_idx`/history semantics, duplicate-ID collapse during assignment, unknown-ID control-flow contamination in `reassign()`, live dict alias leakage, and mutable model-object retention. These are the highest-value additions beyond prior rounds.
